DELIVERABLE: Persist the gateway-assigned or our own client reference before the call; on timeout, set state unknown, and look up that reference in the gateway's message-status API before any repeat. A same-key retry returns the looked-up result (delivered or queued) and never re-sends; only a confirmed not-found allows one resend with the same reference.
BOUNDARY: The reference is stored before each call; no repeat call happens until the status lookup answers, and only confirmed absence permits one new call.
EVIDENCE: Reads the persisted reference, queries gateway status first, replays the stored outcome on same-key retry, and sends again only on confirmed absence.

BOUNDARY: The reference is stored before each call; no repeat call happens until the status lookup answers, and only confirmed absence permits one new call.
EVIDENCE: Lookup by reference precedes any retry; the stored result is replayed on same-key retry.

DELIVERABLE: Mark the row unknown and return 202 with a Location of /messages/{id}; the client polls our resource. The handler stores the state and retries later with the same key, nothing more.
BOUNDARY: State unknown, 202 and a status URL are returned to callers; the key is kept so the same request maps to the same row.
EVIDENCE: Backoff alone is rejected, a status resource is exposed, and the row stays unknown.

BOUNDARY: The reference is stored before each call; no repeat call happens until the status lookup answers, and only confirmed absence permits one new call.
EVIDENCE: Keep the key claimed, persist processor references, run the lookup before a retry, and return the reconciled capture on same-key retry.

DELIVERABLE: On timeout mark the order unknown and return 202 with a status URL; do not release the key. A background worker will later update the order and the client can read the status resource.
BOUNDARY: The key stays claimed and the response is 202 with a status link, so the effect is represented as pending.
EVIDENCE: Shortening timeout is declined; unknown state and status URL are specified.

After a timeout set state unknown and query the carrier's label list or status by that reference prior to any repeat purchase; same-key retry returns the label found (or its pending state) and does not buy again. Re-purchase only if the carrier confirms no label exists for the reference.
BOUNDARY: The reference is stored before each call; no repeat call happens until the status lookup answers, and only confirmed absence permits one new call.
EVIDENCE: Write the reference first, lookup with the carrier before repeating, return the reconciled label on same-key retry, buy anew only after confirmed absence.

EVIDENCE: Event-id-derived reference stored first, processor lookup before repeating, redelivered webhook replays the reconciled outcome, create only on confirmed absence.

EVIDENCE: Persist token before create, query cloud by token prior to retrying, return found instance on same-key retry, create only after confirmed absence.
